text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short, focused periods called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Every day, they hold a quick standup meeting to share progress and discuss any problems. The work itself comes from a backlog, which is a list of tasks or features. These tasks are often written as user stories, describing a need from a customer’s perspective. This makes iterative development possible, meaning the product is improved step by step in each cycle. By receiving feedback after every sprint, teams can adapt quickly and deliver better results.
